prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: acceptance/transfer→screening/sortation/make-up→Outbound Load Control Desk; excludes airline loading. No explicit modes. Elements/flows: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit stages flight-associated bags; Oversize Exception Ticket→Image Resolution Desk confirms authorized oversize position. Bag Tag Printer produces tags/Calibration Witness Tag; replacements require authorized identity confirmation. Flight Data Gateway (Lantern) supplies destination/date/timing; Flight Cutoff Advisory→Baggage Control System (Velvet). Transfer Bag Feeder meters transfers; Late Transfer Bag Card→Bag Reconciliation Station records flight match, sends Bag Match Query. Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight) assigns active lanes, produces Recovery Route Card, applies authorized routing without bypassing screening. Induction Tray Conveyor meters safely. North Gate Scanner (Kestrel) captures/records readable tag/image for identity checks; South Gate Scanner verifies identity, produces Manual Rescan Receipt. Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper) sorts authorized bags, sends Chute Occupancy Note, holds unresolved dispositions. Secondary Inspection Chute controls examination/retention. East Make-Up Conveyor/West Make-Up Conveyor deliver controlled flows. Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard) maintains build positions/order; receives Carousel Release Slip from Airline Ramp Coordinator after flight/position checks. Coordinator confirms staffing/equipment/sequence/flight-side constraints. Outbound Load Control Desk verifies load eligibility/reconciliation. Explosives Response Team (Pebble) handles security examinations/holds; produces Custody Seal Log. Baggage Operations Supervisor (Tern) coordinates Security Duty Manager, Maintenance Technician, airport security personnel, airline ground operations; approves beyond-operator dispositions. Security Duty Manager resolves holds; Maintenance Technician reports restrictions/verifies witnessed calibration before return-to-service. Manual resolution: Image Resolution Desk presents image/exceptions, uses rescan receipt to verify approved second capture. Operator compares features/tag/handling data; requires legibility/certainty, otherwise requests physical inspection. Verify attached physical tag against recorded identity; Velvet checks current routing, authorizes original-path reentry after identity/flight checks. Mismatches hold pending authorized resolution/escalation; revised route/flight requires approval. Requirements: authorized-only access; unsafe/jammed feeds stop; blocked chutes/incomplete/alarmed screening/threats block release pending clearance. Preserve recoverable bag-flight association. Recovery requires location/identity/outcome/authorization agreement. Validate cutoff/route estimates; earlier departures require review; insufficient windows require

New part:
S178: The final disposition and supporting checks are recorded so that later review can trace why the bag returned to the planned process.
S179: Safe operation depends on keeping people clear of moving equipment and maintaining a controlled path for every bag.
S180: The Baggage Operations Supervisor may stop induction when an unsafe condition, uncertain bag location, or loss of control is reported.
S181: A stop command places the affected equipment in a defined safe state without disabling unrelated routes that remain safe to operate.
S182: Before entering a conveyor or sorter hazard zone, the Maintenance Technician isolates the relevant energy sources and verifies that movement has stopped.
S183: Guards and access panels remain in place during operation, and bypasses are permitted only under an approved maintenance procedure.
S184: The Baggage Operations Supervisor uses the occupancy note to confirm that a chute can safely accept bags.
S185: The Maintenance Technician consults the Recovery Route Card before returning equipment to service after a route change.
S186: Pebble secures the response area and directs handling of any bag referred for explosives assessment.
S187: The Security Duty Manager coordinates access control when a security response affects equipment or staff movement.
S188: A scanner fault requires the affected feed to be held until the fault is assessed and the bag disposition is known.
S189: The Maintenance Technician checks for jammed bags, damaged belts, sensor obstruction, and signs of mechanical wear before clearing a fault.
S190: Lantern supplies current flight data so that operating routes can be checked against active assignments.
S191: The Baggage Control System records equipment alarms and presents the affected route for review by authorized personnel.
S192: When the Induction Tray Conveyor stops unexpectedly, staff prevent further bag entry and keep the approach area clear.
S193: The Maintenance Technician removes a jam only after confirming isolation and arranging safe access to the blockage.
S194: The Bag Reconciliation Station supports verification when a bag's location or identity is uncertain after an interruption.
S195: East Make-Up Conveyor runs only after its guards are confirmed closed and its downstream capacity is available.
S196: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit is held from receiving bags when its discharge area is obstructed or its operating status is uncertain.
S197: The Maintenance Technician performs corrective work and reports any condition that prevents safe restart.
S198: The Baggage Operations Supervisor controls the operational hold, communicates its scope, and confirms that affected staff understand the restriction.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
